To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the vagal nerve contains a beta-adrenergic pathway to EC; (b) this vagal pathway causes a release of endoluminal 5-HT from the gut; and (c) vagal nerve stimulation induces a pyloric motor response via ENK- and SPergic mechanisms.

the vagal sympathetic adrenergically mediated release of 5HT from EC is a physiological phenomenon, which may have a physiological role in the control of intestinal motility, and that VIP, ENK and SP are involved in the vagally induced relaxation and contraction of the pylorus, respectively.

the vagus nerve contains a sympathetic adrenergically mediated pathway that causes a release of serotonin from enterochromaffine cells in the small intestine and that the vagus also contains a noncholinergic, nonadrenergic pathway with a relaxatory component (VIP) and two excitatory components (ENK and SP) that control pyloric motor function.

the control of 5-HT release and pyloric motor functions.

the vagus nerve controls 5-HT release and pyloric motor functions via a complex network of adrenergic, cholinergic, VIPergic, ENKergic and possibly SPergic pathways.

the vagal nerve controls 5-HT release and pyloric motor activity by means of different mechanisms, i.e. beta-adrenoceptor and VIPergic pathways.
